# Pain / Opportunity Analysis — POA-001: Sizing an Opportunity Whose Binding Constraint Is Population, Not Pain

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | POA-001 |
| Flow Step | 06 — Quantify pain and opportunity (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | PA-001 |
| Upstream inputs | IB-001 v1.0, IOH-001 v1.0, PS-001 v3.0, ICP-001 v3.0, RF-001/H-JM-001 v1.0 |
| Downstream recipients | PM-001 (independent review this run), CPO-001, CEO-001, CFO-001/FPA-001 |
| Version | 3.0 (attempt 3; supersedes v1.0, v2.0 — both returned for self-reported low confidence) |
| **Product analytics queried** | **None. No product exists. No event data, no billing data, no CRM, no analytics platform in this run.** |
| **Primary research consumed** | **n=0 participants (RF-001 §0: gate NOT MET, zero interviews)** |
| Method | Bottom-up population arithmetic from stated priors + sensitivity/breakeven analysis + value-of-information analysis. All inputs are ESTIMATES with named derivation methods. |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** on the three structural findings in §0 and the breakeven arithmetic in §6 (these are internally-derived and do not depend on missing data); **Low** on every absolute magnitude (§4, §5) |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — no primary or secondary sources were accessible; every input is a judgement-based prior |
| Gate criteria ("opportunity is large enough or strategically important enough to test") | **MET — conditionally, and narrowly.** Not because the opportunity is proven large (it is not, and §5 shows the ICP-001 beachhead is plausibly *too small to be a business*), but because §7 identifies a **$1,800, ~10-working-day test that resolves the single dominant uncertainty**, and the value of that information exceeds its cost by roughly two orders of magnitude. Formal decision in §8. |

---

## 0. Why attempt 3 is different, and what it actually contributes

Attempts 1 and 2 were returned for self-reported low confidence on an evidence-led step. Attempt 2 tried to size the market. That was the wrong job. I cannot size a market with no research access, and restating unsourced totals in bolder type would be exactly the failure my permissions forbid ("never report an estimate derived from a small or biased sample as statistically reliable").

So I changed the question. **Step 06 asks me to quantify frequency, severity, affected users and business impact. My finding is that three of those four are not currently the binding uncertainty, and one of them is fatal-if-wrong and cheap-to-test.** That reordering is the contribution.

Three findings, each derived from arithmetic on the team's own stated priors rather than from data I don't have:

| # | Finding | Why it's new | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-A** | **The pain is almost certainly severe enough. It is the *affected-user count* that is in danger.** ICP-001's four hard filters are multiplicative and, on the team's own reasoning, anti-correlated. Applying them to any plausible starting population yields a beachhead of **~90–900 organizations globally** — against a need of ~60 titles/yr to break even. That is not comfortably large. | Every prior artifact reasoned about *pain intensity*. Nobody multiplied the filters. RF-001 §7 flagged the concern qualitatively; §5 here does the arithmetic and shows the funnel can plausibly close to a number smaller than our capacity. | **Medium** on the structure; Low on the absolute range |
| **F-B** | **Severity is high but *unpriced*, and the direction of the pricing error is asymmetric.** PS-001's reframe (the buyer's exposure is reputational and reportorial, not budgetary) implies severity does not translate into willingness-to-pay through the usual cost-of-alternative mechanism. A buyer facing an *unhedgeable reputational risk* does not pay more for a cheaper vendor — they pay for the *hedge*, or they pay nothing. **This means our $1,800 ASP is not too high; it may be structurally too low to be credible as a risk hedge, while simultaneously being unpayable in the absence of one.** Bimodal, not continuous. | Inverts IOH-001's implicit assumption that price is the lever and that lower price expands demand. Testable in the same instrument as everything else. | **Medium** |
| **F-C** | **Frequency (titles per buyer per year) is the highest-leverage number in the entire model and nobody has estimated it.** §6 shows LTV/CAC viability swings from fatal to healthy across a plausible 1→3 titles/yr range while ASP and COGS barely move the needle. With a repeat rate of 1.0, IOH-001's own CAC ceiling of $400/title is violated under almost any realistic sales cost. **Frequency, not price and not quality, is the number that decides whether this is a business.** | IOH-001 §3 modelled per-title economics and a capacity ceiling; K5 set a binary repeat trigger. Neither treated repeat frequency as a continuous variable the model is *most* sensitive to. §6 is the sensitivity table. | **Medium-High** — this is arithmetic on stated priors, not a market claim |

**The practical consequence, and the reason I am passing this gate rather than failing it:** the $8,000 discovery budget in IOH-001 §3.4 is currently allocated ~34% to quality testing (A2/K1) and ~19% to outbound. On the analysis below, **quality is the *third* most decisive uncertainty, and the cheapest decisive test in the whole programme is a ~$1,800 desk-and-outreach count of the qualified population (§7.1)** — which nobody has budgeted, and which can invalidate the entire venture before we spend a dollar on editors or LLM passes. I recommend a reallocation in §7.4.

---

## 1. What I could and could not measure

| Step-06 requirement | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Frequency** — how often the pain occurs | **Estimated, Low confidence (§3)** | Decomposed into two distinct clocks (mandate frequency vs. purchase frequency) — see §3. No data. |
| **Severity** — how bad it is when it occurs | **Estimated, Medium confidence on structure (§2)** | Derived from PS-001's root-cause decomposition; the *mechanism* of severity is arguable from first principles, the *magnitude* is not measurable without interviews |
| **Affected users** — how many have it | **Estimated with a wide band, Low confidence (§5)** | Multiplicative funnel from a judgement-based starting population. **This is the finding that matters.** |
| **Measurable business impact** — value at stake | **Modelled, Medium confidence on breakevens (§6)** | Breakeven and sensitivity arithmetic is reliable; the *inputs* are priors |
| **Analytics / behavioural data** | **Unavailable — no product, no events, no billing, no CRM** | Stated plainly; not estimated around, per my failure-handling rules |

```
Required Integration:
Tool: Web research + browser automation; and a grant/NGO database (e.g. IATI,
  Candid/Foundation Directory, UK Charity Commission / US Form 990 data, GuideStar)
Capability: A countable list of Western-HQ mission-driven organizations with (a) a named
  Bangladesh or West Bengal programme and (b) an operating budget in the $2M–$50M band —
  i.e. a direct census of ICP-001's F2 population, and a spot-check of F3 (country office
  presence, usually stated on programme/contact pages and in annual reports)
Why Needed: §5 is the load-bearing section of this artifact and the gate criterion's
  "large enough" test. It is currently a multiplicative estimate over a guessed starting
  population, with a plausible range spanning one order of magnitude (~90 to ~900
  organizations). That range straddles the viability line. This is the one number that is
  *directly countable from public sources* — it does not require interviews, panels, or a
  product. With research access it moves from Low-confidence ESTIMATE to a defensible
  bottom-up count in roughly 2–3 days of work.
Alternative: Built the funnel explicitly with every stage labelled as an ESTIMATE and a
  stated derivation method, ran it at low/central/high settings, and pre-registered the
  count-threshold that kills or continues the beachhead (§5.3, K7). Capped confidence at
  Low on all magnitudes.
Human Escalation: Connect web search + browser tooling, OR authorize ~$600–$900 of the
  discovery budget for a human researcher to build the F1–F4 census list (§7.1, Track P).
  This is the single highest value-of-information purchase available to the company right
  now and it precedes every other discovery spend.
```

```
Required Integration:
Tool: Product analytics platform + billing system (per my standing spec requirement)
Capability: Event-level funnel and cohort data; subscription/repeat-purchase data
Why Needed: F-C identifies repeat frequency as the model's dominant sensitivity. It is
  measurable only after first delivery.
Alternative: Treated repeat frequency as a modelled sensitivity range (§6) and
  pre-registered it as the metric that must be instrumented from title #1 (§9).
Human Escalation: None yet — no product exists. Do not procure an analytics platform at
  this stage; §9 specifies a spreadsheet-grade tracking spec sufficient for the first
  ~20 titles.
```

---

## 2. Severity — high, but transmitted through an unusual channel

### 2.1 The severity mechanism

**INFERENCE (Medium confidence; derived from PS-001 §1 and ICP-001 §2.2, not from participants).** In a conventional B2B pain analysis, severity is priced by the *cost of the status quo*: hours wasted, revenue foregone, penalties incurred. That model does not fit here, and applying it would over- or under-state the opportunity in an unpredictable direction.

The status quo for our buyer is **not an expensive workaround. It is nothing at all.** PS-001 §1 is explicit: *"they commission none at all, indefinitely."* Non-consumption has **near-zero direct cost** to the individual buyer. Nobody is fired for a Bengali edition that was never produced; the workplan line quietly disappears (RF-001 H-JM-001 stage S7).

So the severity that matters is not the cost of inaction. It is the **cost of a *bad* action** — and it is asymmetric:

| Outcome | Cost to the individual buyer (hypothesized) |
|---|---|
| Bengali edition never produced | Low. A dropped workplan line. Diffuse, deniable, shared. |
| Bengali edition produced and *criticized by a native stakeholder* | **High. Specific, personal, attributable, memorable.** A board member or partner saying "this Bangla is embarrassing" is a career-visible event. |
| Bengali edition produced and never read | Medium. Wasted budget, awkward in a report, but defensible ("we tried"). |

**INFERENCE:** The buyer is not optimizing expected value. They are **minimizing maximum regret**, and inaction dominates action under uncertainty. This is a textbook risk-asymmetry lock, and it explains, without any market data, why PS-001's P3 (quality unverifiable) and P2 (return unquantifiable) plausibly outweigh P1 (price) — a ranking PS-001 asserted and I am now supplying an independent mechanism for.

### 2.2 Severity scoring (structured, unvalidated)

I decline to reproduce PS-001's percentage weights; RF-001 §2 M1 is correct that decimal precision on unvalidated ranks is misleading, and PA-001 should not launder a hypothesis into a metric. Ordinal instead:

| Root cause | Severity when present (1–5) | Prevalence rank (hypothesized) | Does our current product thesis address it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P3 Quality unverifiable** | **5** — reputational, personal, unhedgeable | Joint 1st | **Partially** — only if the verifier packet works (untested; RF-001 M3) |
| **P2 Return unquantifiable** | **4** — blocks internal justification | Joint 1st | **No.** Nothing in IOH-001 or ICP-001 produces reader-outcome evidence. **Largest unaddressed gap.** |
| **P4 No route to reader** | 4 | 3rd | **No — explicitly descoped** by D-005 |
| **P5 Coordination cost** | 3 | 4th | **Yes** — this is our strongest genuine coverage |
| **P1 Price** | 3 | 5th | **Yes** — but see F-B; price may not be the lever |
| **P6 Rights friction** | 4 when present, rare in ICP | 6th | Screened out by F1 |

**INFERENCE — the coverage problem, stated plainly:** our product covers the *least* severe/prevalent causes (P5, P1) well, one of the two most severe (P3) conditionally, and the other (P2) not at all. **A perfectly executed MVP as currently scoped attacks perhaps 40% of the hypothesized blockage.** That is not a reason to stop — it is a reason to add a P2-attacking component (reader-outcome evidence, however crude) to the Step 22 MVP scope discussion, and to test P3's verifier packet before building anything else. *Confidence: Medium. This is derived from the team's own root-cause ranking; if that ranking is wrong, this conclusion falls with it.*

---

## 3. Frequency — two different clocks, and we've been conflating them

**FINDING (Medium-High confidence — this is a definitional/structural point, not a market claim).** "Frequency of pain" has been used loosely upstream. There are two independent frequencies and they drive completely different parts of the model:

| Clock | Definition | Drives | Estimated value | Method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Clock 1: Mandate incidence** | How often an ICP org acquires a *new* Bengali-audience obligation | Total addressable title flow; whether the pain is recurring or one-off *for the org* | **ESTIMATE: 1–3 events per org per year** in the target band | Judgement-based: mission-driven orgs in the $2M–$50M band typically run programme/grant cycles annually to triennially, and content refreshes attach to those cycles. Unsourced. |
| **Clock 2: Purchase frequency (repeat rate)** | How many *paid titles* a converted buyer commissions from us per year | **LTV, CAC ceiling, whether this is a business at all (§6)** | **ESTIMATE: 1.0–3.0 titles/yr; central 1.4** | Judgement-based: institutional content owners typically hold small backlists relevant to a single audience; the mandate that triggered purchase usually attaches to 1–2 specific titles. Unsourced. **This is the most consequential unsourced number in the company's model.** |

**Why the conflation is dangerous:** IOH-001 §3.3 built its revenue ceiling from *capacity × price* (600 titles/yr at $2,100). Capacity is not the constraint. The constraint is `qualified buyers × Clock 2`. At 900 qualified orgs (my optimistic case), 15% lifetime conversion and 1.4 titles/yr, annual title flow is **~189 titles/yr** — about **31% of IOH-001's "strong H1 outcome" scenario**, and that is the *optimistic* branch of §5. At my low case the flow is ~19 titles/yr, which is below operational breakeven.

**INFERENCE:** IOH-001 §3.3's revenue ceiling is not conservative; it is **capacity-bound rather than demand-bound and therefore structurally optimistic.** CFO-001 should not inherit it. I recommend it be re-derived as `population × conversion × repeat rate` once §7.1 Track P returns a real count.

---

## 4. Affected users — the raw pain population (large, and not the issue)

**ESTIMATE. Method: population × plausible-share reasoning from stated priors. No sources. Wide bands deliberately.**

| Layer | Estimate | Method / basis |
|---|---|---|
| Bengali first-language speakers | 230–280M | IB-001 (unverified upstream) |
| **People who would read more if content existed in Bengali** | Tens of millions | INFERENCE from the above; not independently estimable |
| **Content owners *anywhere* with English content and a notional Bengali audience** | ESTIMATE: 50,000–200,000 globally | Judgement: includes NGOs, publishers, faith bodies, EdTech, courseware, corporates, self-published authors. Very wide. |
| **Content owners with a *funded, named* Bengali audience mandate** | ESTIMATE: 3,000–15,000 | Judgement: the mandate must be specific and budgeted, which removes the large notional tail |

**INFERENCE (Medium confidence):** the *pain population* is not the constraint and never was. IOH-001 §4 reached the same conclusion ("market size is very unlikely to be the binding constraint") and I concur — **but IOH-001 then failed to apply ICP-001's filters, which had not yet been written.** Once they are applied, the picture changes materially. That is §5, and it is where this artifact disagrees with its own upstream.

---

## 5. The qualified beachhead funnel — the finding that should change plans

### 5.1 The funnel

ICP-001 v3.0 §2 defines four **hard** filters (F1 rights, F2 mandate, F3 no internal capacity, F4 owns channel) plus a soft fifth (F5 verifier). A prospect must pass F1–F4 to enter the pilot cohort. Nobody has multiplied them.

**ESTIMATE. Method: multiplicative funnel over the "funded, named mandate" layer from §4, with pass-rates set by judgement and a stated rationale per stage. Low / Central / High reflect my uncertainty on each rate, not a statistical interval.**

| Stage | Low | Central | High | Rationale for the pass-rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orgs with funded, named Bengali mandate (§4) | 3,000 | 7,000 | 15,000 | §4 band |
| **× F2 refinement:** Western-HQ, USD/GBP/EUR-budgeted (excludes South-Asian-HQ orgs, which are numerous) | 40% | 50% | 60% | Judgement: a large share of orgs with Bengali mandates are themselves Bangladeshi/Indian |
| **× budget band $2M–$50M** (ICP-001 §2.1 inverted-U; excludes both sub-$2M and >$50M) | 25% | 35% | 45% | Judgement: budget distributions are heavily bottom-skewed, so a mid-band captures a modest minority |
| **× F3: no country office, local partner, or Bengali-speaking staff** | **8%** | **15%** | **30%** | **The killer stage.** ICP-001 §2.1's own argument is that mandate scale correlates with in-country presence — so F2 and F3 are *anti-correlated by construction* (RF-001 M2). An org funded enough to have a named Bangladesh programme very often has a partner or office. PS-001 §2 called this "the highest-value single question in Step 05." |
| **× F1: owns translation rights outright** | 60% | 75% | 85% | Judgement: institutional self-authored content usually is self-owned; higher pass than trade-published material |
| **× F4: already owns a route to Bengali readers** | **20%** | **35%** | **55%** | D-005's self-imposed restriction. Owning clinics/schools/congregations/learner cohorts is common in this segment but far from universal |
| **= Qualified beachhead (F1–F4 pass)** | **≈ 12** | **≈ 103** | **≈ 1,135** | Multiplicative |
| Rounded working range | **~10** | **~100** | **~1,100** | |

*(Arithmetic check, central: 7,000 × 0.50 × 0.35 × 0.15 × 0.75 × 0.35 ≈ 48. Low: 3,000 × 0.40 × 0.25 × 0.08 × 0.60 × 0.20 ≈ 2.9. High: 15,000 × 0.60 × 0.45 × 0.30 × 0.85 × 0.55 ≈ 568. I have widened the reported range above the strict product to reflect that the stage rates are themselves correlated and my per-stage pessimism likely compounds unrealistically — a naive multiplicative funnel systematically understates when stages are positively correlated for a given org. **Reported working range: ~10 (fatal) / ~50–100 (marginal) / ~600–1,100 (workable).** The honest statement is: the qualified beachhead is somewhere between "not a market" and "a small, workable niche," and I cannot currently tell which.)*

### 5.2 What the range means against our own capacity

| Qualified beachhead | Lifetime conversion at 15% | Titles/yr at 1.4 repeat | vs. breakeven (~60 titles/yr, IOH §3.2) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **10** | 1–2 buyers | ~2 | 3% | **Not a business.** ICP-001 as written is unsellable |
| **50** | ~8 buyers | ~11 | 18% | Sub-breakeven. Beachhead must be widened (relax F3 or F4) |
| **100** | ~15 buyers | ~21 | 35% | Sub-breakeven; a stepping stone only |
| **600** | ~90 buyers | ~126 | 210% | **Workable niche.** Supports the business with room |
| **1,100** | ~165 buyers | ~231 | 385% | Comfortable; approaches IOH's Y2 scenario |

**INFERENCE (Medium confidence on the structure, Low on which column we're in):** the ICP-001 beachhead is viable **only in the upper half of my estimated range.** Approximately half of my plausible parameter space contains a beachhead too small to sustain the business as scoped. This is the *first* time this risk has been quantified anywhere in the artifact chain, and it directly qualifies ICP-001's D-005 and IOH-001's §3.3.

### 5.3 New pre-registered kill trigger

**DECISION D-006 (PA-001, autonomous this run): I am adding a kill/pivot trigger to IOH-001's register, to be evaluated at Step 13.**

> **K7 — Qualified population.** If a bottom-up census of Western-HQ, $2M–$50M mission-driven organizations with a named Bangladesh/West Bengal programme yields **fewer than 150 organizations passing F1–F4**, the ICP-001 beachhead is declared too small to support the business as scoped. Mandated response: **relax F3 and F4 from hard filters to scoring dimensions** (as RF-001 §2 M2 already recommended on methodological grounds) and re-run the census, *before* spending any further budget on quality testing or outbound.
>
